primitives.name: Footpoint-to-Tracklet Correspondence
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `assign_poses_to_players` — footpoint-to-tracklet correspondence; a pose whose ankle midpoint is >60 px from every box is dropped (spectator).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'d_{\\text{ankle}}': 'distance in pixels between ankle midpoint and player bounding box', 'threshold': '60 px'}
primitives.assumptions: Ankle midpoint proximity to player box defines valid pose assignment; spectator poses are discarded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When d_\text{ankle} > 60 px, pose is classified as spectator.

layer2.mapping: Pose assignment maps to tracklet continuity in GSE's motion graph, where spectator poses are excluded from state transition computations.
layer2.telemetry: Number of valid poses assigned per frame, spectator drop rate.

primitives.name: Anthropometric Limb Repair
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `repair_foreshortened_limbs` — anthropometric priors (segment length as a fraction of shoulder width); limbs below 0.45× prior are extrapolated along the visible direction, or mirrored from the contralateral twin when degenerate.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_{\\text{limb}}': 'measured limb length in pixels', 'L_{\\text{prior}}': 'expected limb length as fraction of shoulder width', 'threshold': '0.45'}
primitives.assumptions: Limbs shorter than 0.45× prior are reconstructed using geometric constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When L_\text{limb} < 0.45 × L_\text{prior}, extrapolation or mirroring occurs.

layer2.mapping: Repaired limbs form input for GSE's trajectory estimation kernel, improving motion consistency in low-res frames.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of limbs repaired, average error reduction post-repair.

primitives.name: Full Detect-Crop-Pose-Filter Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `analyse_frame_with_pose` — full detect → crop-pose → correspond → repair → filter pipeline.
primitives.assumptions: Pipeline stages are sequential and each contributes to final pose validity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure at any stage leads to zero valid poses being returned.

layer2.mapping: The pipeline mirrors GSE’s perception-to-action loop, where each stage corresponds to sensor fusion, localization, and filtering.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of pose assignment per frame, stage-wise failure count.
